root_cause.text: The /proc/fs/nfs/exports open handler captures the pointer to the per-network-namespace export cache without taking a reference on the namespace, allowing the namespace to be destroyed and its cache freed while the file descriptor remains open, leading to use-after-free on subsequent reads.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message explicitly states that "exports_proc_open() captures the caller's current network namespace and stores its svc_export_cache in seq->private, but takes no reference on the namespace. If the namespace is subsequently torn down ... nfsd_net_exit() calls nfsd_export_shutdown() which frees the cache. Subsequent reads on the still-open fd dereference the freed cache_detail." The patch adds get_net(net) in exports_net_open and put_net(cd->net) in exports_release to fix the reference counting.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix network namespace reference counting for exports file open/release to prevent use-after-free.
intent_record.what: Added get_net(net) in exports_net_open and introduced exports_release function that calls put_net(cd->net) and seq_release.
intent_record.how: The change increases the network namespace reference count when opening the exports file and decreases it when the file is released, preventing premature namespace cleanup while the file is open.

intent_record.what: Changed the .release member of exports_nfsd_operations from seq_release to exports_release.
intent_record.how: Now, when the file is closed, the custom exports_release function is called instead of the generic seq_release.

candidates.rationale: This statement stores the export cache pointer without first taking a reference on the network namespace (nn), allowing the namespace to be freed while the file is still open and causing use-after-free on subsequent reads.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement assigns the export cache pointer from the network namespace without taking a reference on the namespace. As a result, if the namespace is freed while the file descriptor remains open, subsequent reads will access freed memory, causing a use-after-free vulnerability.
